name: Entity Graph
blurb: Every company, model, paper, person, dataset, benchmark, and regulation as a node.

nodes.scheme: DOI or arXiv id, linked to the original publisher
arXiv id from the model's own tags

reading.body:
Open models outnumber every other node category by an order of magnitude: 15,251 Hugging Face repositories against 396 API models and 269 companies, which means the practical surface area of deployable AI is far larger than the commercial layer suggests.

The graph contains 23,038 nodes in total, spanning entities as structurally different as state bills (2,740), MCP servers (2,051), and hardware entries (37). That last figure is the one worth pausing on. Thirty-seven curated hardware rows sit at the base of a graph that tracks tens of thousands of models and thousands of regulatory instruments. The disparity is not an indexing gap; it reflects the actual shape of the industry, where a thin layer of physical infrastructure supports an enormous and expanding software stack.

The research layer splits in a revealing way: 134 papers are directly tracked, while 1,808 papers appear only because models cite them in their own tags. The site did not surface those 1,808 through editorial judgment; the models themselves nominated them. That distinction matters for anyone using this graph to trace how ideas move from research into deployment. What the data does not cover is weighting, so a paper cited by one obscure model counts the same as one cited by hundreds.
